note:
ISO 2026-W15 runs from April 6 through April 12. Venus and Ceres are separated by about 0.7° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 3.8° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌗 Last Quarter — 04:51:39 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Regulus, Algieba as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -11.5; direct motion; 85.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Apr 11 10:22 UTC. Mercury: Naked eye; magnitude 0.3; direct motion; 53.1% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 93.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Apr 06 19:21 UTC. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 98.6% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 99.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Apr 06 19:21 UTC. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.2; direct motion; 99.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: In solar glare; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: In solar glare; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Apr 11 10:22 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace Sextans’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Sex at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** MCG 9-17-10: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Spindle Galaxy: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Southern Ring Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 3195: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 3201: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; MCG 7-21-37: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.
